tokenizer.name: o200k_base
tokenizer.counted_text: each output file exactly as stored, decoded as UTF-8 (no normalization; line endings and any BOM are kept)
tokenizer.special_tokens: strings such as '<|endoftext|>' are counted as ordinary text: countTokens(text, { disallowedSpecial: new Set() }), like tiktoken's disallowed_special=()

steps: 1. Unicode NFKC: text.normalize('NFKC') (ligatures, full-width forms and no-break spaces become plain characters)
2. Case-insensitive: String.prototype.toLowerCase() (locale-independent Unicode default lowercase mapping)
3. Markdown emphasis and escape characters are deleted: every '*', '_', '\' and '`'
4. Table pipes: every '|' becomes a space, so '|a|b|' and '| a | b |' both read 'a b'
5. NFKC again, so a deletion cannot leave an unnormalized sequence (e.g. 'e', '*', combining acute)
6. Whitespace: every run of JavaScript \s characters (Unicode White_Space incl. line breaks, tabs, NBSP, U+FEFF) becomes one space; the ends are trimmed
normalization.applied_to: the candidate output and every ground-truth string (must_contain phrases, ordered anchors, headings, table cells, noise texts, absent strings) before they are compared
normalization.matching: a check matches when its normalized text is a substring of the normalized output (no word-boundary rule); table cells must be equal after normalization
normalization.not_unified:
nothing else is unified: curly vs straight quotes, dash and hyphen variants, soft hyphens (U+00AD), zero-width characters, HTML entities and
stay distinct; other Markdown syntax ('#', '-', '>', list numbers, link brackets) stays in the text

metric_definitions.text_recall: found / total over checks.must_contain; a phrase is found when its normalized text is a substring of the normalized output. null when must_contain is empty.
metric_definitions.order_score: Each anchor's position is the first occurrence of its normalized text in the normalized output. order_score = length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of the positions of the anchors that were found, taken in ground-truth order, divided by the number of anchors; a missing anchor counts as not in order. not_in_order lists the found anchors outside one such longest subsequence (when several tie, the one patience sorting reconstructs, which ends at the smallest position; ties never change the score). null when ordered is empty.
metric_definitions.heading_recall: Heading lines are CommonMark ATX headings outside fenced code blocks: up to 3 spaces of indentation, 1-6 '#', then a space, a tab or the end of the line; an optional closing run of '#' is dropped. Setext (underlined) headings, bold lines and HTML headings do not count. An expected heading is found when its normalized text is a substring of the normalized text of a heading line; each heading line can satisfy at most one expected heading (maximum one-to-one matching). heading_recall = found / total; null when headings is empty.
metric_definitions.table_recall: The headline table metric. Pipe tables are parsed like GFM tables, outside fenced code blocks: a header line followed by a delimiter line (cells of the form :?-+:?, at least one unescaped '|', the same cell count as the header line), then body lines until a blank line, a line without an unescaped '|', an ATX heading or a code fence (one deliberate difference from GFM: a non-blank line without a '|' right after a table ends it instead of becoming a one-cell row); body rows are padded with empty cells or cut to the header width; '\|' does not split cells. For each expected table, every parsed table is scored: (a) columns are paired by equal non-empty normalized header text, one-to-one, left to right; (b) each other expected column is paired by position, keeping the column offset of the nearest header-paired column (looking left first, then right; offset 0 when no column was paired by header), if that column exists and is free; (c) expected columns still unpaired take the remaining free columns left to right; (d) rows, header rows included, are aligned in order by dynamic programming to maximize the number of matching cells. A matching cell is an aligned pair of cells with equal, non-empty normalized text. Cells that are empty after normalization are not counted on either side. recall R = matching cells / non-empty expected cells; precision P = matching cells / non-empty cells of the parsed table; F1 = 2PR / (P + R), 0 when P + R = 0. Separately for each expected table, the parsed table with the highest recall is picked; ties on recall go to the higher precision, then to the earliest table in the output. A parsed table with no matching cell is never picked: when no parsed table has a matching cell (or the output has none), R = P = F1 = 0 and no table is named. table_recall = mean R over expected tables. null when tables is empty.
metric_definitions.table_precision: Secondary. Mean P over expected tables, each P taken from the same parsed table that table_recall picked. Precision is secondary because an expected table can be partial: it may list only some rows of a larger source table, so a complete, faithful conversion carries correct cells beyond the expected ones, and they lower precision. null when tables is empty.
metric_definitions.table_f1: Secondary. Mean F1 over expected tables, each F1 computed on the same parsed table that table_recall picked (so it is not the best F1 over all parsed tables). Secondary for the same reason as table_precision. null when tables is empty.
metric_definitions.noise_excess: For each noise entry, count the non-overlapping occurrences of its normalized text in the normalized output; excess = max(0, count - max). noise_excess = sum of the excesses. null when noise is empty.
metric_definitions.absent_violations: Number of absent entries whose normalized text occurs in the normalized output (each entry counts once). null when absent is empty.
metric_definitions.size: chars = Unicode code points of the output file as stored; bytes = its UTF-8 bytes; tokens = o200k_base tokens of the same text (see tokenizer). A missing output is empty: 0 / 0 / 0.
metric_definitions.aggregates: Macro averages: for each candidate, the mean of each per-file score over the files where that check applies (n). Missing outputs are scored as empty text and included. For tables, table_recall is the headline number (the tblRec column of the stderr summary); table_precision and table_f1 are kept beside it as secondary fields. noise_excess and absent_violations give their total and mean per file; chars and tokens give totals and means. complete_files = files where every candidate produced an output; tokens.total_on_complete_files sums tokens over those files only, and tokens.ratio_vs_markitdown_on_complete_files divides it by markitdown's sum on the same files.
metric_definitions.rounding: Non-integer numbers in the report are rounded to 6 decimal places when written; means are computed from unrounded values.

files.notes: Federal Register PDF exactly as served by govinfo (4 pages, Federal Register pages 106231-106234, three text columns per page). Ground truth was built from the rendered pages (each page read as an image, tables re-checked at 200 dpi); pdftotext was used only to check the exact characters of strings. Reading order: page 1 starts with the masthead and the boxed section note in column 1, then column 1, column 2, column 3; tables span the full width between column blocks. Several must_contain phrases deliberately cross a column boundary on the same page: 'revisions to the / fee structure' (page 1, column 2 to column 3), '$317.50 inspection fee will be / determined' (page 2, column 1 to column 2 below Table 1) and 'subject / to such actions' (page 2, column 1 to column 2 at the foot of the page). No phrase crosses a page boundary. Line-end hyphens are written joined: '40,000-pound' and 'per-pound' are true compounds and keep their hyphen (both are printed unbroken elsewhere in the document); the absent entries are the split forms a converter leaves when it keeps a line-end hyphen and joins the lines with a space, listed only where the joined word is one unhyphenated word on the page ('in- spection' and 'Agricul- tural' in the Table 1 and Table 3 footnotes, 'Destina- tion' in the redesignation table on page 4). Every line-end hyphen in the body text of this document falls inside a true compound ('per-pound', '40,000-pound'), so no body-text split form is listed as absent. Headings are the document title (the SUBJECT line) plus the section headings and the CFR part and section headings of the amendatory text; the agency, sub-agency, CFR, docket and RIN lines of the preamble are bold labels and are not listed. The two section-symbol headings are given without the leading '§'/'§§' because the text layer has no space after the section sign while the page shows a thin space; each listed string is an exact substring of the printed heading. In '51.39 through 51.62 [Redesignated as' the page shows a wide space before '[', which the text layer encodes as an 8-point positioning gap with no space character. Table captions are not headings. Noise: 'Vol. 89, No. 249' is VISIBLE: it is printed once in the page-1 masthead (legitimate) and again in the running header of pages 2-4, so a faithful conversion has 1. 'Jkt 265001' is INVISIBLE: it belongs to GPO's production slug ('VerDate Sep<11>2014 ... Jkt 265001 ... 30DER1', set horizontally along the bottom edge in white), which exists in the text layer of all 4 pages but is not visible on the rendered page, so a faithful conversion has 0; max 1 is used as the lenient running-header/footer limit, and 'Jkt 265001' is used instead of 'VerDate Sep<11>2014' because converters may escape the angle brackets. A second invisible slug, 'ddrumheller on DSK120RN23PROD with RULES1', is set rotated (also in white) in the left margin; it is not checked because extractors emit rotated text inconsistently (forwards, reversed or split), so a count would penalize only the converters that read it forwards. Tables: both listed tables are complete, every header and body row as printed (Table 1: 8 rows including the '(1)'-'(3)' column-number row; Table 3: 12 rows including the '1'-'5' column-number row); Table 2, Table 4 and the redesignation table on page 4 are not listed. Table 1: the 'New fee' header carries a superscript footnote marker, written as '¹' (NFKC-normalizes to '1'); the row-1 'Reduced cost' value is printed '$0.' with a period, as are the other values in that column. Dot leaders after cells are not part of cell text; the last two cells of the '9 commodities' row in Table 3 hold only dot leaders and are empty. Table 1's footnote prints '$0.00605' where the body says '$0.00635'; this inconsistency is in the source and no check depends on it. Page 4, column 3 ends with the first part of an unrelated Nuclear Regulatory Commission final rule ('Non-Power Production or Utilization Facility License Renewal'), which is part of this PDF as published; it is not listed among the headings or checks. AUDIT 2026-11-24: removed absent entry 'per- pound' because 'per-pound' is a true compound (printed unbroken elsewhere), so its line-end split is not a one-word hyphenation artifact (policy 6); replaced a note that cited one converter's output for the rotated slug with a tool-neutral reason; noted that 'Vol. 89, No. 249' is visible and 'Jkt 265001' invisible (white text), that both tables are complete, and the gap before '[Redesignated as'. Re-verified every other item against the rendered pages (Tables 1 and 3 and the page-4 headings at 200 dpi) and the text layer: no change needed; must_contain phrases are continuous in reading order, 9-26 words, occur once, cross no link and only the line-end hyphen of the certain compound '40,000-pound'; no item contains the file name or converter-added text; no ordered anchor is footnote text; all headings are bold stand-alone lines; sha256 unchanged.

files.notes: Senate committee report PDF exactly as served by govinfo (10 pages: PDF page 1 is the cover, page 2 the committee roster with printed folio '(II)', page 3 is report page 1, and PDF pages 4-10 carry printed page numbers 2-8). Ground truth was built from the rendered pages (each page read as an image, the CBO table re-checked at 200 dpi); pdftotext was used only to check characters. Headings and names printed in small capitals match case-insensitively, so they are written in ordinary case where the page uses small caps. All ordered anchors are body text (PDF pages 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10), none is footnote text, so where a converter places footnotes (after the page body, before it, or at the end of the document) does not change order_score; the anchors test reading order across pages. The text layer of PDF page 4 stores footnotes 1-9 before the page's body text; footnote text is checked only by must_contain (footnotes 2 and 6 on PDF page 4). Line-end hyphens are written joined where the page breaks a word ('require-ments', 'au-dits', 'find-ings', 'des-ignated'); compounds keep their hyphen ('Government-wide', 'grant-by-grant'). The absent entries are split forms a converter leaves when it keeps a line-end hyphen and joins lines with a space (PDF page 3 'require- ments', PDF page 4 'per- sistent', 'effec- tiveness' and 'chal- lenges'). The 'Contents' heading is set in small capitals; the table of contents repeats the Roman-numbered section titles with page numbers, so no ordered anchor uses a section title. The cost-estimate summary box at the top of PDF page 7 ('S. 4716, Financial Management Risk Reduction Act ... * = between zero and $500,000.') is an embedded image with no text layer and is not checked. The cover page and report page 1 both print the title, 'Calendar No. 519' and 'Report 118-226' as legitimate content; they are not running headers. The only visible running header is the page number, too short to count, so noise lists GPO's production slug 'VerDate Sep 11 2014 ... Jkt 049010 ... SR226', set horizontally along the bottom edge, which is in the text layer of all 10 pages but not visible on the rendered page (the only noise entry, and it is invisible: it exists only in the text layer): a faithful conversion has 0, and max 1 is used as the lenient running-header/footer limit. A second invisible slug, 'jgilmore on DSK126QN23PROD with REPORTS', is set rotated in the left margin of every page; it is not checked because extractors emit rotated text inconsistently (MarkItDown 0.1.9 emits it reversed, e.g. 'DORP32NQ621KSD'), so a count would penalize only the converters that read it forwards. Other hidden text-layer strings ('E:\Seals\Congress.#13' on the cover, 'Insert offset folio 9 here SR226.001' on PDF page 7) are not checked. In the statute text on PDF page 9 the bold brackets marking omitted law are printed as brackets but come out of the text layer as 'ø' and '¿', and the closing mark on PDF page 10 is a circle that comes out as 'Æ'; no check depends on these glyphs. The CBO table (Table 1, PDF page 8) is covered completely except for its spanner: the header row is the year row (empty stub cell, then 2024 to 2029 and '2024–2029'), followed by both body rows ('Estimated Authorization' and 'Estimated Outlays'). The spanner 'By fiscal year, millions of dollars—' (em dash), printed centred over all seven year columns, is not a table row: a one-header-row Markdown table has no objectively right column for a spanning cell, and as the first expected row it would steer the scorer's header-based column pairing. It is not a must_contain phrase either, because the image-only summary box on PDF page 7 prints 'By Fiscal Year, Millions of Dollars', which an OCR step would match case-insensitively. The last column header is printed on two lines as '2024–' / '2029' (en dash) and is written joined, like '2025–2029' in the text; row labels are written without their dot leaders. 'TITLE 10—MONEY AND FINANCE' is printed as shown, although the amended section is in title 31. The heading 'UNITED STATES CODE' (PDF page 9) is a short string that also occurs in the cover line 'TO AMEND SECTION 7504 OF TITLE 31, UNITED STATES CODE, ...'; it is kept because it is printed as a bold display heading. AUDIT 2026-11-24: re-read all 10 pages as images (Table 1 and the SEC. 7504 heading at 220 dpi) and checked every item; sha256 unchanged. Changes: (1) must_contain 'GOVERNMENTAL AFFAIRS UNITED STATES SENATE TO ACCOMPANY S. 4716' -> 'COMMITTEE ON HOMELAND SECURITY AND GOVERNMENTAL AFFAIRS UNITED STATES SENATE', because the old phrase ran across three differently styled cover lines (large caps, small-caps 'TO ACCOMPANY', larger 'S. 4716') where a converter may legitimately start a new heading; the new phrase is one same-styled block that occurs only on the cover. (2) ordered anchor 'Thirty Years from Initial Legislation' removed: it is footnote 2 text, and its position relative to body text depends on where a converter places footnotes, which is a convention, not an objective reading order (7 body-text anchors remain). (3) Table 1: the spanner row ['', 'By fiscal year, millions of dollars—', '', ...] removed and the year row made the header row: the spanner's column in a Markdown table is a convention (it is printed centred over all seven year columns, its middle near the 2027 column, not over 2024), and as row 0 it decided the scorer's header-based column pairing, so a converter that placed it under its centre would have had every column shifted. (4) notes updated to match. All other items were verified against the rendered pages and kept: must_contain phrases are continuous text in reading order, at least 6 words and unique, the line-end hyphen joins ('require-ments', 'au-dits', 'find-ings', 'des-ignated') are certain single words, and no phrase crosses a link (the PDF has no link annotations; URLs are plain text); the headings are all display headings (centred small-caps Roman-numbered titles and 'Contents', italic 'Section n.' lines set on their own, bold statute headings); the four absent split forms are true line-end breaks of single words that never occur legitimately; no check contains the file name or depends on converter-added text (the PDF Title metadata is empty).
